summary.intent: Extract shared-write operations from the web UI's useSharedNavigation hook into stateless SDK functions, covering the 5 recipient-side write handlers plus updateSharePermission, with comprehensive test coverage.
summary.outcome: The GSD quick task was initialized and a plan was created at .planning/quick/260327-2ab-extract-shared-write-operations-from-web/260327-2ab-PLAN.md. Execution had not yet completed at the end of the transcript.

repo: The SDK currently only exposes owner-perspective share operations (shareFolder, revokeShare, reWrapForRecipients); the entire recipient write path is missing from the SDK and lives only in the web UI hooks.
useSharedNavigation.ts contains ~400 lines of framework-agnostic crypto/IPFS/IPNS business logic tangled with React state (useState, useRef, useCallback) that needs extraction.
publishSharedFolderMetadata (~line 719 of useSharedNavigation.ts) is the recipient-side counterpart to the SDK's updateFolderMetadataAndPublish — uses re-wrapped IPNS key instead of owner key.
The SDK's ShareCallbacks type uses 'file' | 'folder' but the web UI has expanded ShareKeyType to 'file-ipns' | 'folder-ipns' — types need widening.
withRevocationGuard (~line 761) and isForbiddenError (~line 140) implement a revocation detection pattern needed by any SDK consumer doing shared writes.
uint8ToBase64 helper in the web UI is a duplicate — already exists in sdk-core as a utility.

code.finding: publishSharedFolderMetadata — recipient-side IPNS publish, analogous to SDK's updateFolderMetadataAndPublish but uses re-wrapped key
withRevocationGuard — wraps write operations to catch 403 and transition to read-only; needed pattern for SDK consumers
isForbiddenError — detects share revocation via 403 response
refreshFolderContents — resolves IPNS, decrypts shared folder metadata, returns children + sequence number; shared-folder variant of sdk-core's fetchAndDecryptMetadata
updateSharePermission — thin wrapper around sharesControllerUpdatePermission; natural addition to SDK share module

workflow: The analysis phase (identifying SDK candidates) was done inline by the assistant before invoking the GSD quick workflow, rather than using --research flag — appropriate since the codebase analysis was already complete.
GSD quick task ID format is YYMMDD-xxx (Base36 2s precision), e.g. 260327-2ab.
Quick task directories are created at .planning/quick/{quick_id}-{slug}/ separate from phase planning directories.
